title: Drug-fuelled melee subject of inquest; HIV-positive transsexual died after being dragged from building
article: "Watch out, she bites."
With those words, George Draper backed away slowly from the hysterical woman with the long, dark hair and let the police officers handcuff her and take her into custody.
She had appeared in the eighth-floor stairwell of his Sanford Avenue North apartment a little after 9 p.m. She was holding a broom and shouting something barely coherent about being chased by dogs.

Draper and another tenant, Walter Berry, had come running to see what was the matter. They arrived in time to see the woman trip over her broom stick and tumble down the concrete steps to the landing below.
Draper charged down the steps to help the woman to her feet. That was when he saw the knife. He grabbed the weapon from her and handed it to Berry's wife, Wendy.

"It got much worse after that," said Draper, who told a coroner's inquest yesterday about the wild fracas that ensued and how the woman bit him several times, including one painful bite to his shoulder that drew blood.
"I don't know if I'm allowed to tell this or not," said Draper. "But she had AIDS and I'm still getting blood work every five or six months. But so far, everything is OK."
Dr. Darryl Wolski and the coroner's jury are examining the death on Feb. 20, 2003, of Abdirhman Ali Abdi, 26, who was known on the streets of Hamilton by the female identity, Chevranna.
The HIV-positive transsexual died in police custody after being handcuffed, then carried and partly dragged down more than seven floors of stairs.
Forensic pathologist Dr. Chitra Rao, who conducted the post- mortem examination, concluded the cause of death was inhalation of vomit brought on by cocaine poisoning.

Walter Berry, who is missing an arm, left his wife to help Draper restrain the woman, before he ran to get the superintendent. The woman yanked Wendy Berry's hair and nearly pushed her down a flight of stairs. Wendy and Draper fought to control the flailing woman for five or more minutes until two police officers, having hiked up the stairs, came to their rescue.
John Waters, a building superintendent, said the elevators had been out of service for two weeks.
"It was chaos," said Waters of the melee he observed after returning with Walter Berry to the stairwell.

He said Abdi was not a tenant but had been staying with a man on the eighth floor. Waters said he noticed Abdi coming and going from the building and suspected she was either a prostitute or a drug dealer.
"This was not a nice building," Waters said.
"The hallways were dingy and disgusting. Either she was doing sexual favours or dealing drugs. She would come and go with different men."

Hamilton police Constable Michael Page said he found hypodermic needles and cocaine paraphernalia in the eighth-floor apartment where Abdi had been staying. He also found vials of pills that were prescribed for her.

Constable Dennis Bryson said he and Constable Oliver Mann struggled to carry the woman, who was ranting and thrashing about. On their way down to the ground floor, they became fatigued and had to release her legs, letting her lower limbs drag while they carried her upper body face down.
Mann said Abdi gradually became more docile as they approached the lobby. He saw her vomit slightly on two occasions. But in the front vestibule, he could see she was not breathing.
Mann got a barrier valve from the patrol car and he began blowing into Abdi's mouth, while Bryson did chest compressions.

Their efforts at resuscitation were followed by firefighters who arrived with a defibrillator. Ultimately, a complete advanced cardiac life support was carried out by advanced-care paramedic Blake Mills.
Abdi was pronounced dead in the trauma unit of Hamilton General Hospital at 10:20 p.m.
Coroner's counsel James Ramsay and Marco Visentini, legal counsel for the Hamilton Police Service, are to make closing remarks today.
